newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Genting says revenue hit by Singapore row.
newsitem.headline: Genting says revenue hit by Singapore row.

text.p: Malaysian casino and resorts operator Genting Bhd said on Wednesday its revenue for the current financial year had been adversely affected by a political spat between Malaysia and Singapore earlier in 1997.
"We have noted a slight dip in receipts from Singapore (clients) since the little spat," Mohammed Hanif Omar, Genting's deputy chairman told reporters after the company's annual general meeting.
The row in March was sparked by Singapore Senior Minister Lee Kuan Yew's remarks in a court affidavit that Malaysia's Johor state was "notorious for shootings, car-jackings and muggings".
Hanif said currently around 36 percent of the occupants of the casino resort's hotels in Genting Highlands just outside Kuala Lumpur, were from Singapore.
An official later confirmed that the figure had been higher before the row broke out, but declined to give any figures.
Hanif added that receipts had picked up during the recent Good Friday holiday period, and that the "impact would only be temporary".
